title: ChannelScheme picks your side of the sync relationship: CONNECT polls, SWITCHBOARD pushes
content:
Sync between two reactors is asymmetric, and `ChannelScheme` is how you declare which end you are:

```typescript
enum ChannelScheme {
  CONNECT = "connect",
  SWITCHBOARD = "switchboard",
}
```

`ChannelScheme.CONNECT` selects `GqlRequestChannelFactory` — the client side, which polls for inbound operations and pushes its own outbound ones. `ChannelScheme.SWITCHBOARD` selects `GqlResponseChannelFactory` — the server side, which is push-driven and does not poll.

The two factories have different constructor shapes, and the reason is instructive: `GqlRequestChannelFactory` takes `(logger, jwtHandler, queue)` while `GqlResponseChannelFactory` takes only `(logger)`. The request side needs the queue because polling applies **backpressure** — a tick defers when the reactor queue depth exceeds `maxQueueDepth`. The response side has no timer to throttle, so it needs neither.

Two consequences follow from the asymmetry:

- `withJwtHandler` only flows through the `CONNECT` factory. On the `SWITCHBOARD` path it is accepted and **ignored** — the server does not authenticate outward, it authenticates inbound callers. The handler signature is `(url: string) => Promise<string | undefined>`, called per request with the target URL.
- `ISyncManager.triggerPull(name)` on a `GqlResponseChannel` is a **no-op**, because there is nothing to pull; that channel is push-driven by design.

Today GraphQL over HTTP is the only shipped transport, and the channel config `type` string is `"gql"` for both sides. `GqlResponseChannel` and its factory are Switchboard-side primitives relevant to `reactor-api` wiring rather than typical app code — application developers pick `CONNECT` almost every time.

The docs flag one instability here: `IChannelFactory.instance`'s `cursorStorage` and `operationIndex` parameters are marked for removal in source, so do not depend on the factory signature staying fixed.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/04-Reference/01-Reactor/04-Synchronization.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
description: CONNECT builds GqlRequestChannelFactory (polling client), SWITCHBOARD builds GqlResponseChannelFactory (push server). withJwtHandler flows only through CONNECT.
